points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 1840年11月12日，奥古斯特·罗丹出生于巴黎一个普通家庭。父亲是警察局职员，母亲是裁缝。尽管家庭并不富裕，但父母支持他的艺术兴趣。罗丹从小就展现出对绘画和雕塑的天赋，经常在笔记本上涂鸦。这段时期，他接触到了古典艺术作品，特别是卢浮宫中的雕塑，这些早期经历奠定了他后来艺术风格的基础。然而，他的学业表现平平，尤其是数学和科学课程，这导致他多次被学校开除。
points.descriptionEn: On November 12, 1840, Auguste Rodin was born in Paris to a working-class family. His father was a police clerk and his mother a seamstress. Despite modest means, his parents supported his artistic interests. Rodin showed early talent for drawing and sculpture, often sketching in notebooks. During this period, he was exposed to classical artworks, particularly sculptures in the Louvre, which laid the foundation for his later artistic style. However, he struggled academically, especially in math and science, leading to multiple expulsions from school.

points.title: 艺术求学
points.description: 1854年，14岁的罗丹进入巴黎装饰艺术学校学习，但很快因过于写实而与学院派风格产生冲突。1857年，他参加巴黎美术学院的入学考试，但连续三次失败，这成为他艺术生涯的重要转折点。此后，他转向实用艺术，为装饰艺术家工作，同时坚持创作。这一时期，他受到米开朗基罗作品的深刻影响，并开始发展自己独特的风格。1864年，罗丹创作了第一件重要作品《伤鼻男子》，展示了他对人物心理状态的深刻把握。普法战争期间，他参军服役，这段经历对他后来的创作产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1854, at age 14, Rodin entered the École des Arts Décoratifs, but soon clashed with academic styles due to his realistic approach. In 1857, he failed the entrance exam for the École des Beaux-Arts three times, becoming a pivotal moment in his career. He then turned to decorative arts while continuing to create independently. During this period, he was deeply influenced by Michelangelo's work and began developing his distinctive style. In 1864, Rodin created his first significant work, 'The Man with the Broken Nose,' demonstrating his profound understanding of human psychology. During the Franco-Prussian War, he served in the army, an experience that profoundly influenced his later work.

points.title: 比利时时期
points.description: 1871年，罗丹移居比利时，为布鲁塞尔的装饰艺术家工作。在布鲁塞尔的九年间，他创作了《青铜时代》、《施洗者约翰》等重要作品，并开始形成自己独特的艺术语言。1875年，罗丹前往意大利研究米开朗基罗的作品，这次经历对他产生了决定性影响。1877年，《青铜时代》在巴黎沙龙展出，却因过于写实而被指控为从真人直接翻模，引发巨大争议。这一时期，罗丹还开始创作《地狱之门》的初步构思，这部作品将成为他一生的重要工程。在布鲁塞尔，罗丹还遇到了未来的伴侣罗丝·贝雷，这段关系对他的生活和创作都有深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1871, Rodin moved to Brussels, where he worked as a decorative artist. During his nine years in Belgium, he created important works such as 'The Age of Bronze' and 'John the Baptist,' and began developing his distinctive artistic language. In 1875, Rodin traveled to Italy to study Michelangelo's work, an experience that proved decisive for his development. In 1877, 'The Age of Bronze' was exhibited at the Paris Salon but caused controversy due to its realism, with accusations that it was cast directly from a live model. During this period, Rodin also began preliminary work on 'The Gates of Hell,' a project that would occupy him for much of his life. In Brussels, he also met his future companion Rose Beuret, a relationship that profoundly influenced both his life and work.

points.title: 艺术巅峰
points.description: 1880年，罗丹返回巴黎，接受委托创作《地狱之门》，并获得了工作室。这一时期，他的艺术风格完全成熟，创作了大量杰作，包括《思想者》、《吻》、《巴尔扎克》等。1884-1887年，他创作了《加莱义民》，这是他最具代表性的公共纪念碑之一。1890年代，罗丹的艺术声誉日益增长，获得了多项荣誉，包括1891年被授予荣誉军团勋章。1900年，巴黎世界博览会为罗丹举办了大型个人展览，确立了他在国际艺术界的地位。晚年，罗丹继续创作，同时培养了许多年轻艺术家，如布德尔、马约尔等。1913年，他捐赠了自己的全部作品给法国政府，建立了罗丹博物馆。1917年11月17日，罗丹在巴黎逝世，与相伴一生的罗丝·贝雷合葬。
points.descriptionEn: In 1880, Rodin returned to Paris, commissioned to create 'The Gates of Hell' and given a studio. During this period, his artistic style fully matured, and he produced numerous masterpieces including 'The Thinker,' 'The Kiss,' and 'Balzac.' From 1884-1887, he created 'The Burghers of Calais,' one of his most representative public monuments. In the 1890s, Rodin's artistic reputation grew, earning numerous honors including being made a Chevalier of the Legion of Honour in 1891. In 1900, the Paris World Exposition hosted a major retrospective of Rodin's work, establishing his international status. In his later years, Rodin continued to create while mentoring young artists such as Bourdelle and Maillol. In 1913, he donated all his works to the French government, leading to the establishment of the Musée Rodin. Rodin died in Paris on November 17, 1917, and was buried alongside his lifelong companion Rose Beuret.

points.title: 晚年岁月
points.description: 1916年，罗丹在巴黎郊区的默东购买了别墅，作为他的工作室和住所。这里成为他晚年创作和生活的中心。尽管健康状况日益恶化，罗丹仍然坚持创作，完成了《教堂》系列等作品。在这一时期，他开始整理自己的艺术理念，为后人留下了宝贵的艺术思想。默东的别墅后来成为罗丹博物馆的一部分，保存了大量他的手稿、素描和雕塑作品。在这里，罗丹回顾了自己一生的艺术探索，思考艺术与生命的关系。这段最后的岁月虽然短暂，但充满了创作活力和哲学思考，为他的艺术生涯画上了圆满的句号。
points.descriptionEn: In 1916, Rodin purchased a villa in Meudon, a suburb of Paris, which served as his studio and residence. This became the center of his later life and creative work. Despite declining health, Rodin continued to create, completing works such as his 'Cathedral' series. During this period, he began organizing his artistic philosophy, leaving behind valuable artistic thoughts for posterity. The Meudon villa later became part of the Musée Rodin, preserving numerous manuscripts, sketches, and sculptures. Here, Rodin reflected on his lifelong artistic exploration and contemplated the relationship between art and life. Though brief, these final years were filled with creative energy and philosophical thought, bringing his artistic career to a fitting conclusion.

supporter.zh: 罗丹被誉为现代雕塑的先驱，他打破了传统雕塑的束缚，开创了表现主义雕塑的先河。他的作品强调内在情感和生命力的表达，而非单纯的完美形式。罗丹对雕塑语言的革新影响了后世无数艺术家，被誉为米开朗基罗之后最伟大的雕塑家。他坚持艺术创作的自由，拒绝被学院派规则所限制，这种精神激励了后来的现代艺术运动。罗丹的作品如《思想者》、《吻》等已成为人类文化遗产的重要组成部分，他的艺术理念至今仍对当代艺术产生深远影响。
supporter.en: Rodin is hailed as a pioneer of modern sculpture who broke free from traditional constraints and pioneered expressive sculpture. His works emphasize the expression of inner emotions and vitality rather than mere formal perfection. Rodin's innovations in sculptural language have influenced countless artists throughout history, earning him the title of the greatest sculptor since Michelangelo. He upheld creative freedom, refusing to be limited by academic rules, an ethos that inspired later modern art movements. Works like 'The Thinker' and 'The Kiss' have become essential parts of human cultural heritage, and his artistic philosophy continues to profoundly influence contemporary art.

critic.zh: 批评者认为罗丹的作品过于注重表面效果而缺乏内在深度，有时被指责为哗众取宠。他的某些作品如《巴尔扎克》因不符合传统审美标准而引发争议，甚至被拒绝展出。罗丹的个人生活也备受争议，他与多位女性模特的关系以及对待助手的态度都受到批评。此外，一些艺术评论家认为罗丹后期作品质量下降，重复使用早期主题，缺乏创新。他的商业成功也被一些人视为艺术妥协的表现，认为他为了迎合市场而牺牲了艺术纯粹性。
critic.en: Critics argue that Rodin's works sometimes prioritize surface effects over inner depth, accused of sensationalism. Certain pieces like 'Balzac' sparked controversy for deviating from traditional aesthetic standards and were even rejected for exhibition. Rodin's personal life also faced criticism, particularly his relationships with multiple models and his treatment of assistants. Additionally, some art critics contend that his later work declined in quality, recycling earlier themes without innovation. His commercial success has been viewed by some as artistic compromise, suggesting he sacrificed artistic purity for market appeal.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，罗丹被定义为连接古典与现代艺术的关键人物。他既继承了文艺复兴时期对人体的深刻理解，又开创了现代雕塑的表现形式。罗丹的作品已成为文化符号，《思想者》尤其在全球范围内被广泛认可，代表着人类沉思的状态。他的艺术理念强调捕捉瞬间和情感，这一方法影响了后来的表现主义和抽象艺术。罗丹博物馆作为他最重要的遗产之一，保存了大量作品和手稿，为研究他的艺术思想提供了宝贵资源。在当代艺术教育中，罗丹被视为艺术创新与传统的完美结合，他的作品被世界各大博物馆收藏和展示。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Rodin is defined as a pivotal figure bridging classical and modern art. He inherited the Renaissance's profound understanding of the human form while pioneering modern sculptural expression. His works have become cultural symbols, with 'The Thinker' achieving global recognition as an icon of human contemplation. His artistic emphasis on capturing moments and emotions influenced later expressionist and abstract movements. The Musée Rodin, his most significant legacy, preserves numerous works and manuscripts, offering invaluable resources for studying his artistic philosophy. In contemporary art education, Rodin is viewed as the perfect fusion of innovation and tradition, with his works collected and exhibited by major museums worldwide.

self.zh: 艺术是孤独的产物，因为它是心灵对自然的沉思。
self.en: Art is the result of a solitary meditation, for it is the contemplation of nature by the mind.

others.zh: 罗丹是雕塑界的莎士比亚，他不仅创造了形式，还创造了思想。
others.en: Rodin is the Shakespeare of sculpture; he not only created forms but also created thought.
